newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: US ambassador to Prague slightly injured in crash.
newsitem.headline: US ambassador to Prague slightly injured in crash.

text.p: The U.S. ambassador to the Czech Republic, Jenonne Walker, escaped serious injury when her chauffeur-driven Cadillac was involved in a crash as she travelled to a charity event, the U.S. embassy in Prague said on Wednesday.
Walker, 62, was riding in the rear seat on Tuesday evening when according to local media, her Czech driver failed to give right of way to a van while turning from the main road.
The van ploughed into the side of the car. Pictures from the scene of the accident showed a deep dent from the impact on the door where the ambassador was sitting.

"She suffered some minor injuries but she's certainly in the office, hard at work (on Wednesday)," embassy spokeswoman Jocelyn Greene told Reuters, adding that Walker had a bruised lip and various abrasions.
The driver of the van was treated for injuries at a local hospital and released and Walker's driver was not hurt. Police are still determining who was at fault, Greene said.
The diminutive Walker did not go to hospital but went directly home instead of continuing on to the charity fashion show she was scheduled to attend, Greene added.
Embassy officials said that if not for the strength of the Cadillac's construction, the ambassador may have been more severely injured.
Walker took her Prague post in mid-1995 after serving on President Bill Clinton's National Security Council following her service as an analyst for the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA).
